# Additive ordered two/three-reference source fixtures

These artifacts extend the frozen v2 one/four-reference oracle without replacing any historical fixture, weights, adapter, input, numerical bound, or source implementation. `multi_receipt.json` records the exact Python/Torch/diffusers environment, scheduler hash, all five unchanged historical artifact hashes, and exact replay of the original BF16 and represented-weight F32 one/four-reference trajectories before new outputs were written.

`fixture.json` uses the same source extraction, nonzero rank-two adapter, mixed-aspect reference tensors, masks and scheduler as v2, with capture counts two and three. It includes original-coordinate projections, t0 modulation, K/V, positive/negative cached and uncached predictions, timestep trajectories, and wrong-time/visibility/order controls. `fp32_sampler.json` independently executes the unchanged frozen source with exactly represented BF16 weights widened to F32.

Native comparisons retain the original bounds: exact projections/coordinates and cached/uncached native equality; BF16 `max(abs(expected))/64 + 1/1024`, mutants separated by more than three times that bound; complete represented-weight F32 sampling `2e-5`, mutants separated by more than 100 times that bound; actual F32 CFG/Euler arithmetic `1e-6`. Complete BF16 trajectory drift remains diagnostic only.

The generator runs externally beside the original hash-frozen upstream source directories, following the existing fixture convention. It has no native output inputs. This proves source fixture provenance only; tiny transformer comparisons do not constitute public RGB-to-image execution, real-weight quality, or measured device peak acceptance.

Approved before native execution: two-reference reversed-order BF16 source separation is 0.09228515625, below the unchanged three-bound threshold 0.19482421875. That new control is retained as a diagnostic; native executes the actual reversal, compares it to source at the original BF16 bound and requires nonidentical output. Two-reference order acceptance composes exact ordinal coordinates with the unchanged strict-F32 full-trajectory bound 2e-5 and original 100-times mutation threshold 0.002; source reversal separation is 0.04332876205444336. Two-reference BF16 correct predictions, t0/visibility controls and every original one/four and new three-reference BF16 gate retain their original bounds. No source artifact, weight, input or tolerance was changed to fit a backend.
